description: Internal ICP (ideal customer profile) scoring for LaunchTrace's own supplier prospects. This decides who to approach first. It is a prioritisation aid, not a prediction: a Priority A prospect is one worth ten minutes of research, nothing more. Every weight here is editable, and every score comes back with the reasons that produced it.
precision_note: Scores are derived from text the operator wrote about each prospect. They are only as good as that text. Treat a 5-point difference as noise.
band_note: Score at or above the threshold lands in that band. Below the C threshold, or any hard-suppress rule, gives SUPPRESS. The A threshold is set so that Priority A is roughly a fortnight of careful outreach rather than a label almost nobody earns; it is a working-set size, not a claim about quality.
category_weight_note: How well LaunchTrace's signal matches what this supplier sells. Packaging, co-packing and contract manufacturing are what an emerging brand buys first, so a new-brand signal is worth most to them.

positive_signals.label: Explicitly markets to startups or challenger brands
Low minimum order quantities or short runs, so a first-time brand can actually buy
Food or FMCG specialism rather than general industry
Sells something a new consumer brand buys repeatedly, not once
Has a sales or business-development function to act on a lead
Sells across the UK rather than to one town
Small or mid-sized, so one new brand is financially meaningful
Member of a relevant trade body, so takes the sector seriously
Corporate identity is verifiable (limited company, LLP or PLC)
A usable business contact route is already recorded

negative_signals.label: Serves only very large contracts, so a first-time brand is not a customer
No clear food or FMCG relevance
Local consumer-facing business, not a supplier to brands
Very large business where a £79/month feed is likely immaterial
No commercial sales function to receive a lead
Corporate identity could not be confirmed
Website was never confirmed, so the record may be wrong

hard_suppress.description: Conditions that force SUPPRESS regardless of score. These are safety rules, not scoring.
hard_suppress.opted_out: The prospect asked not to be contacted.
hard_suppress.status_suppressed: The prospect is already marked SUPPRESSED.
hard_suppress.not_trading: The business is recorded as dissolved or no longer trading.
hard_suppress.no_company_name: No company name, so nothing can be verified.
